trace: To develop a systematic equity trading strategy exploiting seasonality in the Indian market, we aim to capitalize on known calendar effects. The primary focus will be on identifying stocks with historically higher returns during specific months or quarters. Economic mechanisms underlying this could include variations in investor behavior (e.g., tax-driven selling in end-of-year periods), seasonal changes in economic indicators (e.g., agricultural performance affecting rural stock markets), and company-specific events (e.g., earnings announcements). These effects might persist due to predictable patterns in investor sentiment, corporate activities, and macroeconomic conditions. The rule would involve constructing a calendar-based portfolio that allocates investments according to the observed seasonality, buying stocks during months with positive historical returns and selling them as these periods end, thus capturing potential alpha.

To develop the systematic equity strategy, the primary signal will be based on historical returns of stocks during specific months. The process involves calculating monthly returns for each stock over a multi-year historical period (e.g., 10 years) using daily closing prices. On any given day, we rank stocks by their average positive returns in historically favorable months. Candidates are then selected to construct the calendar-based portfolio by choosing those with the highest average month-end returns during targeted months. This ranking helps identify stocks that have historically performed well at certain times of the year, leveraging known seasonal effects in the Indian market.

For this systematic equity strategy, we propose holding a portfolio of approximately 30-50 stocks to balance diversification and manage complexity. Position weights will be dynamically adjusted based on the average historical returns during targeted months, with no single stock accounting for more than 4% of the total portfolio value to limit individual risk exposure. The overall portfolio risk is managed by setting a maximum allowable loss threshold of ±10% per month to ensure sustainable performance and reduce drawdowns. This approach helps in capturing seasonal effects while maintaining robust risk management practices.
